recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-11915 unless a future TSMG or Vocabulary decision explicitly changes FHIR ValueSet OID allocation, which should be handled as a separate issue.
issue_request: Published FHIR-core vocab issue resolved Persuasive with Modification, requesting correction of the generated OID shown for the 2016Sep Common Languages ValueSet, where the ballot page exposed 2.16.840.1.113883.4.642.2.languages and raised confusion with BCP47/RFC5646 language-tag identifiers and the older 2.16.840.1.113883.6.121 OID.
initial_application: Jira described this as a publishing issue and recorded that the specification was correct while the ballot output was wrong. No Git commit message directly mentions FHIR-11915, but git pickaxe shows 06af2eaa68a07b473d22ea80f85e8404a762307b, 'rebuild value set OID system', removing urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113883.4.642.2.languages from source/terminologies/valueset-languages.xml; later published releases use numeric FHIR ValueSet OIDs instead.
additional_context: Current source/terminologies/valueset-languages.xml defines http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/languages with urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113883.4.642.3.20 as the primary identifier and urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113883.4.642.3.891 as an old identifier, with source/oids.ini mapping the URL to .3.20. The all-languages ValueSet uses .3.21. build.fhir.org reports the same identifiers. A broader Jira search found FHIR-26606, but that issue was retracted and concerns a v3/THO HumanLanguage ISO/IETF reference rather than this generated FHIR ValueSet OID.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current authoritative source and current generated build no longer contain the reported textual .2.languages OID; changing the present numeric mapping would not be supported by FHIR-11915.

related_jiras.note: Later retracted issue about Human Language ISO/IETF references in a v3/THO context; it does not affect the FHIR-11915 generated-OID conclusion.
